A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ROIDA. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching content moved into the main text in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original ROIDA evaluations on D4RL locomotion and manipulation tasks, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and statistical summaries.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds a PU-learning ablation, loss-weight sensitivity experiments, and a reward-selection visualization.

M1.justification: The PU reward model, reward filtering, weighted behavioral cloning, TD learning, and combined policy objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated, and the newly tested variants are experimental controls rather than revisions to ROIDA.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four MuJoCo and four Adroit environments using the same expert and auxiliary datasets. New diagnostics reuse existing tasks. The revised rliable task pool changes aggregation within retained coverage; HalfCheetah remains evaluated elsewhere.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators BC-exp, BC-all, DemoDICE, ORIL, DWBC, and BCDP are retained. V3 Table 3 adds a binary-classification reward-learning control, labeled 'w/o PU learning', absent from the corresponding v2 Table 4.

E3.justification: V3 introduces the binary-classification control and one-at-a-time alpha/beta sweeps from 0.001 to 1.0 on Hopper 5/5. Appendix A.3 also describes nine locomotion tasks rather than Appendix F's twelve, omitting HalfCheetah from that aggregate. The unchanged rliable plots do not establish recomputation.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands diagnostic validation: Table 3 directly tests the central PU-learning component across locomotion settings, Appendix A.4 tests both loss weights, and Appendix A.5 examines ground-truth reward distributions by predicted class. Existing threshold, scalability, ground-truth-reward, and eta analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and averages over the last ten evaluations. The rliable median, mean, IQM, optimality-gap metrics, and 95% confidence-interval convention remain unchanged. No new repeated-run count or uncertainty-estimation procedure is disclosed.

E6.justification: V3 adds PU-ablation results, including Hopper's 83.19 ± 10.64 without PU learning versus the retained ROIDA result of 86.58 ± 16.42, and findings in Figures 6–7. Matched existing tables retain their numerical values. Figure 1's redraw changes the returns implied by its bars without corresponding Table 1 updates.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, mathematical assumptions, reward formulation, Bellman operator, and objectives in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Neither version adds distinct theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: combining PU learning with weighted cloning and TD learning enables robust use of auxiliary demonstrations of varying quality. The additional diagnostics support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly identifies the current implementation as single-task and discusses multi-task or goal-conditioned extensions. V2 instead proposes future learning from multimodal inputs on physical robots. Existing reward-estimation and class-prior limitations are retained, with relocation into the main text.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access URL in the abstract and documents selecting the 0.01 loss-weight factors using Hopper 5/5 experiments. The architectures, dynamic loss balancing, learning rates, optimizer, discount factor, and GPU information were already disclosed in v2 Appendix D.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to DemoDICE, DWBC, BCDP, DICE methods, and offline RL remain unchanged. Author-year citations, added bibliographic URLs, and numbered related-work subsections are presentation changes.

P1.justification: V3 extensively reorganizes the main text and appendices, moving pseudocode, manipulation expert-size results, detailed ablations, limitations, and broader impacts into the main paper. Appendices are regrouped as A.1–A.5, and experimental discussion is revised, although much underlying prose is retained.

P2.justification: The two-column document becomes a single-column journal layout. V2 Tables 2 and 6 merge into v3 Table 2; ablation displays are consolidated and expanded; several tables move; Figures 6–7 are added. Figure 1 is redrawn with its return axis starting at 50 rather than 60. The merged Table 2 retains a locomotion-only caption.

improvement.justification: The new PU control and Hopper diagnostics strengthen validation of existing design choices, while the code link and explicit single-task limitation improve access information and scope clarity. These gains are limited because the principal benchmark evidence was already present. The unexplained Figure 1 redraw and the merged Table 2's stale caption partially offset the improvements.
